title: Chest pain at work
dispatch: Medic 4 is dispatched non-emergent to an office for a 58-year-old with chest discomfort.
scene: The patient is seated in a break room, alert, anxious, and speaking in full sentences. A coworker is present. No hazards are identified.
history: Substernal pressure began 25 minutes ago while carrying boxes
Pain is 7/10, constant, and radiates to the left arm
Associated nausea and diaphoresis; denies shortness of breath
History of hypertension and high cholesterol
Takes lisinopril and atorvastatin
No known drug allergies
findings: Alert and oriented to person, place, time, and event
Breathing regular and unlabored; lungs clear bilaterally
vitals: Initial: BP 156/92, HR 104 regular, RR 18, SpO2 97% room air, BGL 118 mg/dL
Repeat after care: BP 148/88, HR 92, RR 16, SpO2 98%; pain 3/10
care: Placed on cardiac monitor and 12-lead ECG obtained
324 mg chewable aspirin administered after confirming no allergy or active bleeding
Transported in position of comfort with ongoing reassessment
response: Pain decreased from 7/10 to 3/10. Skin remained cool but diaphoresis improved.
disposition: Transported non-emergent to the emergency department. Verbal report and care transferred to the receiving RN.

title: Asthma with respiratory distress
dispatch: Ambulance 12 is dispatched emergent to a residence for difficulty breathing.
scene: A 24-year-old is found sitting upright on a couch, leaning forward, and speaking in three-to-four-word sentences. The scene is safe.
history: Wheezing began about one hour ago after visiting a home with cats
History of asthma
Used albuterol inhaler twice without relief
Denies chest pain, fever, recent illness, and known medication allergies
findings: Diffuse expiratory wheezes with diminished bases
vitals: Initial: BP 138/84, HR 118, RR 30 labored, SpO2 91% room air
After treatment: BP 134/82, HR 110, RR 22, SpO2 96%; speaking in full sentences
care: Oxygen administered per local protocol
Albuterol nebulizer administered per local protocol
Continuous monitoring and repeat lung-sound assessment
response: Work of breathing decreased, aeration improved, wheezing remained mild, and the patient could speak in full sentences.
disposition: Transported to the emergency department in position of comfort; care transferred to ED staff with report.

title: Altered mental status from hypoglycemia
dispatch: Medic 7 is dispatched to a grocery store for a confused person.
scene: A 66-year-old is seated on the floor with store staff nearby. No trauma or hazards are identified.
history: Staff report the patient became sweaty and confused while shopping
Patient has diabetes and uses insulin
Patient skipped lunch
No known drug allergies
Denies pain after mental status improves
findings: Initially responds to verbal stimuli and is oriented only to person
Airway patent with intact gag and ability to swallow
No focal neurologic deficit or signs of trauma
vitals: Initial: BP 132/76, HR 96, RR 16, SpO2 98%, BGL 42 mg/dL
After treatment: BP 128/74, HR 84, RR 16, SpO2 98%, BGL 86 mg/dL
care: Oral glucose administered after confirming ability to swallow
Patient reassessed after treatment and given food supplied by family after improvement
response: Patient became alert and oriented to person, place, time, and event; diaphoresis resolved and BGL increased to 86 mg/dL.
disposition: Patient agreed to transport for evaluation. Care and report transferred to the receiving RN.

title: Suspected opioid overdose
dispatch: Ambulance 3 is dispatched emergent to a public restroom for an unconscious person.
scene: A 31-year-old is found supine. A bystander reports possible fentanyl use. Drug paraphernalia is present but is not handled by EMS. Law enforcement has secured the scene.
history: History is limited
Bystander reports the patient was last seen awake approximately 10 minutes earlier
Allergies, medications, and medical history are unknown
findings: Unresponsive to voice with response to painful stimulus
Airway partially obstructed by relaxed tongue
Skin pale and cyanotic around lips
vitals: Initial: BP 108/64, HR 58, RR 6 shallow, SpO2 78% room air, BGL 102 mg/dL
After ventilation and naloxone: BP 122/70, HR 88, RR 16, SpO2 96%
care: Airway repositioned and suction prepared
Ventilations provided with BVM and oxygen
Naloxone administered per local protocol
Continuous airway and respiratory reassessment
response: Respiratory rate and oxygenation improved. Patient became responsive to voice and maintained the airway but remained drowsy.
disposition: Transported emergent to the emergency department; care transferred to ED staff.

title: Postictal patient after seizure
dispatch: Medic 2 is dispatched emergent to a park for a reported seizure.
scene: A 40-year-old is found lying on the grass. A spouse states generalized shaking lasted about two minutes and stopped before EMS arrival.
history: Known seizure disorder
Missed the morning dose of levetiracetam
No reported trauma
No known drug allergies
Spouse denies recent fever or illness
findings: Initially responds to verbal stimuli and is confused
Airway patent with small amount of oral secretions
No obvious trauma; moves all extremities
vitals: Initial: BP 146/86, HR 108, RR 20, SpO2 94% room air, BGL 112 mg/dL
Repeat: BP 138/82, HR 94, RR 18, SpO2 97%
care: Positioned to protect airway
Oxygen administered per local protocol
Monitored for recurrent seizure and reassessed neurologically
response: No recurrent seizure. Patient became alert and oriented to person, place, and event but remained unsure of the exact time.
disposition: Transported non-emergent for evaluation; report and care transferred to ED staff.

title: Possible acute stroke
dispatch: Medic 9 is dispatched emergent to a residence for sudden weakness.
scene: A 72-year-old is seated at a kitchen table with a spouse. The scene is safe.
history: Spouse reports sudden speech difficulty and right-sided weakness
Last known well was 14:10; EMS contact at 14:34
History of atrial fibrillation and hypertension
Takes apixaban and metoprolol
No known drug allergies
findings: Right facial droop and right arm drift
Left grip strong; right grip weak
Airway patent; breathing unlabored; lungs clear
vitals: Initial: BP 188/104, HR 92 irregular, RR 18, SpO2 96%, BGL 124 mg/dL
Repeat: BP 184/100, HR 90 irregular, RR 18, SpO2 97%
care: Stroke alert initiated with receiving facility
Last-known-well and anticoagulant use communicated
Head elevated and patient monitored; no oral intake
response: Neurologic deficits remained unchanged during transport.
disposition: Transported emergent to a stroke-capable facility; bedside handoff included last-known-well, anticoagulant use, glucose, and exam findings.

title: Abdominal pain with vomiting
dispatch: Ambulance 6 is dispatched to a residence for abdominal pain.
scene: A 35-year-old is found seated on a bathroom floor beside a toilet. The scene is safe.
history: Right-lower-quadrant pain began gradually eight hours ago and is now 8/10
Pain worsens with movement
Three episodes of non-bloody vomiting
Denies diarrhea, urinary symptoms, chest pain, and shortness of breath
No significant medical history; no medications; allergic to penicillin
findings: Abdomen tender in the right lower quadrant with guarding
vitals: Initial: BP 118/72, HR 104, RR 20, SpO2 99%, temperature 100.8°F
Repeat: BP 116/70, HR 100, RR 18, SpO2 99%
care: Position of comfort
Nothing by mouth
Emesis bag provided and patient monitored
response: Pain remained 8/10 with no additional vomiting during transport.
disposition: Transported non-emergent to the emergency department; report and care transferred to receiving staff.

title: Fall with hip injury
dispatch: Medic 5 is dispatched to a residence for an older adult who fell.
scene: An 81-year-old is found on the bedroom floor. The patient reports tripping over a rug. Family witnessed the fall.
history: Landed on the left side
Denies loss of consciousness, head strike, neck pain, and back pain
Left hip pain is 9/10
Takes warfarin for atrial fibrillation
No known drug allergies
findings: Left leg shortened and externally rotated
Tenderness at left hip without open wound
Distal pulse, movement, and sensation present before and after movement
vitals: Initial: BP 164/88, HR 96, RR 18, SpO2 97%
Repeat: BP 158/84, HR 90, RR 16, SpO2 98%
care: Patient moved with scoop stretcher and positioned for comfort
Left lower extremity supported
Cold pack applied with skin protected
Distal neurovascular status reassessed
response: Pain decreased to 6/10 after positioning and support. Distal status remained intact.
disposition: Transported non-emergent; care transferred to ED staff with anticoagulant use emphasized.
requiredFacts: distal status before and after movement

title: Two-vehicle collision
dispatch: Ambulance 10 is dispatched emergent to a two-vehicle collision at an intersection.
scene: Fire personnel have blocked traffic. One 29-year-old driver remains seated in a sedan with moderate front-end damage. No intrusion or airbag deployment is noted.
history: Restrained driver traveling approximately 25 mph
Denies loss of consciousness
Reports midline neck pain and left knee pain
Denies chest pain, shortness of breath, abdominal pain, numbness, and weakness
No medical history, medications, or allergies reported
findings: Airway patent; breathing normal; lungs clear
Skin warm and dry; pulses normal
Abrasion and swelling to left knee
Distal pulse, movement, and sensation intact in all extremities
vitals: Initial: BP 142/86, HR 92, RR 18, SpO2 98%
Repeat: BP 138/82, HR 88, RR 16, SpO2 99%
care: Manual cervical stabilization maintained during assessment and movement
Patient assisted from vehicle according to local protocol and secured on stretcher
Cold pack applied to knee with skin protected
response: No change in neurologic status. Knee pain decreased from 6/10 to 4/10.
disposition: Transported non-emergent to the emergency department; report and care transferred to the receiving RN.

title: Cardiac arrest with ROSC
dispatch: Medic 1 is dispatched emergent with fire personnel to a residence for a person in cardiac arrest.
scene: A 63-year-old is found supine in the living room. Family states the patient collapsed approximately four minutes before EMS arrival. Bystander CPR is in progress.
history: Witnessed collapse with immediate bystander CPR
History of coronary artery disease
Medication and allergy details unavailable during resuscitation
findings: Unresponsive, apneic, and pulseless on EMS arrival
High-quality CPR performed with minimal interruptions
After ROSC: airway supported, bilateral breath sounds present, skin pale and cool
vitals: After ROSC: BP 104/68, HR 112, RR assisted 12, SpO2 95%, ETCO2 38 mmHg, BGL 136 mg/dL
Repeat: BP 110/72, HR 104, SpO2 96%, ETCO2 36 mmHg
care: Defibrillation and medications provided according to local cardiac-arrest protocol
Advanced airway and waveform capnography used
Post-ROSC ECG obtained
Hemodynamics, oxygenation, ventilation, and neurologic status continuously reassessed
response: Sustained ROSC with palpable pulses through transfer of care; patient remained unresponsive.
disposition: Transported emergent to a cardiac-capable facility with prearrival notification; resuscitation record and care transferred to ED team.
